sources.method: The Computer History Museum's printed centimetre triple (sources[0], «9.21w x 8.89h x 11.75l (cm)») x 10: width 92.1, height 88.9, depth 117.5 mm; exact decimal shift, no rounding added.

notes: Source: Computer History Museum record 102718237, «Odyssey 2 joystick», 1978, Magnavox Consumer Electronics Company, a single joystick (not a boxed set). The record prints «3 5/8w x 3 1/2h x 4 5/8l (in)» and «9.21w x 8.89h x 11.75l (cm)»: the inch triple is the museum's measurement at 1/8 in resolution and the cm triple is the museum's own printed metric figure; the mm values restate that printed cm triple ×10, filed with a derived source naming the method (the brief treats any unit change as a derivation). Axes as CHM labels them: w → width, h → height, l (length) → depth; the record does not say whether the lever is included in h (it most likely is) or whether the cord is excluded, so excludes_projections is null. The CHM weight «1 (lb)» is a whole-pound rounding and is not used. Controls: the Odyssey² owner's manual (archive.org odyssey2ownersmanual1980) does not describe the joystick, so controls is an uncovered []. Whether a unit is hardwired (early consoles) or plugged is not stated by either source: wired null.
